goal: Decide whether a change to a UOR Foundation repository may be made, by whom and by which route, so that no remediation writes to a repository without its owners' go-ahead.

app.name: uor-remediation-write
app.title: Remediation write policy
app.purpose: Decide, as an XACML 3.0 policy decision point, whether a remediation change may be written to a UOR Foundation repository, from who acts, what kind of change it is, the repository's state, whether an Organization Owner approved it, and the route it takes.

fields.name: actor
fields.means: who acts: an Organization Owner, a software agent that acted on behalf of an owner (PROV-O actedOnBehalfOf), a Repository Maintainer, anyone else, or an actor whose identity cannot be verified

fields.name: change
fields.means: the kind of change: a file in the repository, a topic tag, a branch ruleset, or a repository rename

fields.name: repository
fields.means: whether the repository is live or archived on GitHub

fields.name: approval
fields.means: whether an Organization Owner approved this remediation

fields.name: route
fields.means: a pull request to the default branch, or a direct write

meanings.permit: XACML 3.0 section 7: the policy applies and allows the change
meanings.deny: XACML 3.0 section 7: the policy applies and forbids the change
meanings.not-applicable: XACML 3.0 section 7: no rule of the remediation policy applies, because the actor is not part of the remediation
meanings.indeterminate: XACML 3.0 section 7: the policy could not be evaluated, here because the actor's identity cannot be verified

rules.why: PROV-O: an agent's acts are attributed through actedOnBehalfOf; an actor whose identity cannot be verified cannot be attributed
GOVERNANCE.md (UOR-Foundation/.github@92da114114fc9b76cbf2c5168e29d409b62ddde8) 4.1: the remediation is an act of the Organization Owner, Repository Maintainers and agents acting for them
GOVERNANCE.md (UOR-Foundation/.github@92da114114fc9b76cbf2c5168e29d409b62ddde8) 11: an archived repository is a read-only historical state; it takes no pull request
GOVERNANCE.md (UOR-Foundation/.github@92da114114fc9b76cbf2c5168e29d409b62ddde8) 4.1: the Organization Owner makes final governance decisions; no remediation is written without the owner's go-ahead
GOVERNANCE.md (UOR-Foundation/.github@92da114114fc9b76cbf2c5168e29d409b62ddde8) 3 and 7.1: review before merge, no direct pushes; a change is a pull request linked to an issue
GitHub: topics, rulesets and repository renames are repository settings that need admin permission, which only an Organization Owner holds
GitHub: a repository setting is not carried by a pull request; the owner applies it directly

app.otherwiseWhy: GOVERNANCE.md (UOR-Foundation/.github@92da114114fc9b76cbf2c5168e29d409b62ddde8) 4.1 and 7.1: an approved file change by pull request, or an approved setting applied by an Organization Owner

properties.why: an agent never writes without an owner's go-ahead
a file change always goes through review
an agent never changes branch protection
an approved agent opens the file pull request

stakeholders.name: Organization Owner
stakeholders.text: Approves the remediation and applies the settings only an admin can change, and needs no write to happen without that approval.

stakeholders.name: Agent contributor
stakeholders.text: Opens the remediation pull requests on behalf of the Organization Owner and needs to know exactly which changes it may make and how.

stakeholders.name: Repository Maintainer
stakeholders.text: Reviews each remediation pull request and needs every change to arrive through review, never as a direct push.

components.name: GitHub repository settings
components.text: The topics, rulesets, names and files of each UOR-Foundation repository.

components.name: Remediation register
components.text: remediation/project.mjs and remediation/register.json in UOR-Foundation/community, which project each repository's change set from the decision apps.

components.name: GitHub App credentials
components.text: The scoped token an agent writes with: contents and pull requests, never administration.

threats.name: Write without approval
threats.text: An agent opens or pushes remediation changes the Organization Owner never approved.

control.name: Owner go-ahead
control.text: Any actor other than the owner is denied without approval.

evidence.reference: Alex's go-ahead in the community project thread, 2026-11-14

threats.name: Protection weakened by an agent
threats.text: An agent with a broad token changes or removes a branch ruleset.

control.name: Settings are the owner's
control.text: Topic, ruleset and rename changes by anyone but the owner are denied.

threats.name: Unreviewed push
threats.text: A file change lands on a default branch without a pull request.

control.name: Pull request only
control.text: A direct file write is denied.

threats.name: Spoofed agent
threats.text: An actor claims to act for the owner without a verifiable delegation.

control.name: Unverified is indeterminate
control.text: An actor whose identity cannot be verified gets indeterminate, never permit.

threats.name: Credential leaked in a pull request
threats.text: A token or secret is committed with a remediation file.
threats.accepted: Remediation files are generated from public data (SPDX text, CODEOWNERS logins, workflow YAML) and carry no secret; GitHub secret scanning covers the rest.

threats.name: Mass pull requests flood maintainers
threats.text: Thirty repositories each receive a remediation pull request at once and review stalls.
threats.accepted: One small pull request per repository, each linked to its issue and its change set, keeps every review a single read.

quality.text: Every permitted change names the owner who approved it and the agent that acted for them.
quality.measureText: Permitted changes without an approving owner.

quality.requirement: Protection changed only by the owner
quality.text: No rule permits a ruleset change by anyone but the owner.
quality.measureText: Rules that permit a setting change by a non-owner.
